transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I suppose it’s mostly that I’ve been feeling… foggy, mentally. I don’t want to make too much of it, but at work I’m having trouble keeping my place in my old cataloguing notes, and sometimes I just sort of sit there not quite able to decide what simple thing to do next. It’s a bit embarrassing, honestly.
How long have you been experiencing this fogginess and difficulty with decision-making?

I’d say… about three months, give or take. It’s been there most days, the low mood and the fogginess. I first really noticed it around when I started getting ready to leave the library. It’s not every single minute, but it’s been fairly steady, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed during this time?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but most days lately I end up sitting at the kitchen table and it feels like the color’s gone out of things a bit. Even my old watercolor books, which I usually enjoy, just make me feel kind of heavy rather than interested. If that’s the sort of thing you mean.
Have you experienced any thoughts of death or suicidal ideas during this time?

I… no, I don’t think so. Not in the sense of making plans or wanting to do anything to myself. I may have had a passing thought like, “I’m tired of feeling this way,” but I wouldn’t call it suicidal. I hope that makes sense.
Have you noticed any significant loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yes… I suppose I have. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but things I used to like just don’t pull me in the same way. I’ll sit at the kitchen table most days and it’s like the color’s gone out of everything a bit. Even my old watercolor books… instead of being enjoyable, they just feel kind of heavy. Is that what you mean?
Would you say your low mood is consistently worse than a mild feeling of being down?

I think… yes, probably more than just mild. I keep wanting to say it’s not that bad, but most days lately I’m just sitting at the kitchen table feeling like the color’s gone out of things. Even looking at my old watercolor books doesn’t really lift me up — it just feels heavy. So, yes, I guess I’d say it’s more than just being a little down.
Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns over the past three months?

A little, yes… mostly with eating, I think. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I do have to sort of remind myself to eat sometimes. My wife has noticed I’ll leave my rice or soup half-finished, and I never used to waste food like that. Is that the kind of change you mean?
Would you describe your low mood as feeling hopeless?

Hopeless… I don’t know if I’d use that word all the time. I don’t want to overstate it. But most days lately I do just sit at the kitchen table and everything feels sort of drained, like the color’s gone out of it. Even my old watercolor books, which I used to enjoy, just make me feel heavy instead of interested. So… maybe not completely hopeless, but it does feel pretty bleak sometimes.
Would you say there are any days where your low mood is significantly worse than others?

I’m not sure it changes a lot day to day, exactly. There are some days that feel heavier than others, yes, but mostly it’s this… steady dullness lately. I end up sitting at the kitchen table and it feels like the color’s gone out of everything. Even looking through my old watercolor books doesn’t really catch my interest — it just makes me feel kind of heavy. Does that answer what you mean?
Would you say there are days where you feel like you're unable to experience any pleasure at all?

I wouldn’t say every single day is like that, no… or maybe I’m trying not to make it sound too dramatic. But most days lately, I end up just sitting at the kitchen table and it’s like the color has gone out of everything. Even my old watercolor books — things I used to enjoy — I look at them and they just make me feel heavy instead of interested. So… yes, I guess there are times where pleasure feels pretty far away.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or that you look forward to?

I wish I could say there was more I looked forward to. I mean, I still pick up my old watercolor books sometimes, thinking maybe they’ll get me interested again, but most days lately I just end up sitting at the kitchen table feeling like the color’s gone out of everything. They don’t really give me pleasure right now… they mostly just make me feel heavy. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say there are days where you feel completely unable to experience any pleasure at all?

Yes… I think there are days like that. I don’t want to overstate it, but most days lately I just end up sitting at the kitchen table, and it feels like the color has gone out of everything. Even my old watercolor books don’t really pull me in anymore — they just make me feel heavy instead of interested. So… yes, I guess sometimes it feels like I can’t really feel pleasure at all.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure most of the day, nearly every day?

I think… yes, most days lately it’s been that way for a good part of the day. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I do end up sitting at the kitchen table a lot, just feeling like the color’s gone out of everything. Even my watercolor books don’t really interest me — they just feel heavy to look at. Is that what you’re asking?
Would you say your low mood is present for most of the day?

Yes… I think it is, most days. I try not to make too much of it, but lately I spend a lot of the day just sitting at the kitchen table feeling like the color’s gone out of everything. Even my old watercolor books, which used to help a little, just make me feel kind of heavy now. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but most days lately I’m just sitting at the kitchen table, and things feel kind of… drained of color. Even my old watercolor books, which I used to like looking through, just feel heavy now instead of interesting. So yes, I guess it’s most of the day, nearly every day.
Would you say your low mood is interfering with your ability to function in daily life?

Yes… I think it is, more than I’d like to admit. I’m still trying, but I’ve let things pile up — lecture plans, travel notes, even simple household paperwork. It’s embarrassing, because I used to be able to organize myself pretty reliably, and now I just… don’t seem to get it together the same way. Is that the kind of functioning you mean?
Would you say your low mood is significantly impacting your daily life, such as affecting your relationships or work performance?

Yes… I suppose it is. I don’t want to overstate it, but I’ve let things pile up — lecture plans, travel notes, even simple household paperwork — because I just can’t seem to organize myself reliably the way I used to. It feels embarrassing to say that, but yes, it is affecting my day-to-day life.
Would you say your low mood is severe enough that it's nearly always on your mind?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I mean, I try not to sit there dwelling on it on purpose, but most days lately I end up at the kitchen table and it’s like the color has gone out of everything. Even my old watercolor books — which should be comforting, I suppose — just make me feel heavy instead of interested. So… yes, it does seem to be there nearly all the time.
